text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower in quiet dealings. May lost $0.80 to close at $305.50 per tonne, while August gave up $0.20 to close at $305.00 per tonne. The May arbitrage widened out to around $68.50, with sellers said to be waiting in the wings at $69 and above. Interest was noted in the further forward premiums but the rangebound levels were discouraging actual trades.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed lower across the board on speculative liquidation of long positions. Trade buying was brisk at the lows, which supported the spot month. May lost 13 points to close at 10.75 cents/lb, while July ended 8 points lower at 10.53 cents/lb. Speculators have apparently come to the conclusion, that current fundamentals do not allow a significant rise in world market prices.

MOZAMBIQUE - Sugar production in Mozambique in 1996/97 (May/April) is forecast to reach 34,000 tonnes, tel quel, up from 29,288 tonnes produced in 1995/96 and 28,351 tonnes produced in 1994/95. Sugar consumption in 1995/96 was put at 68,000 tonnes, up from 60,000 tonnes in 1994/95.

BRAZIL - Sugar exports picked up somewhat in January reaching a total 464,464 tonnes, raw value, up from 395,265 tonnes in December 1996 and 353,876 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first three quarters of 1996/97 (May/January) up to 4.970 mn tonnes compared to 5.473 mn tonnes in 1995/96.

Total exports in 1995/96 reached the record high of 5.922 mn tonnes compared to 4.352 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in May/January 1996/97 were Nigeria with 431,940 tonnes whites against 318,096 tonnes, Algeria with 303,350 tonnes compared to 289,285 tonnes, Egypt with 286,919 tonnes, down from 516,604 tonnes and Russia with 272,449 tonnes against 560,251 tonnes.

The largest raw sugar destinations in 1996/97 were the United States with 177,945 tonnes against 105,194 tonnes, Russia with 101,900 tonnes compared to 423,296 tonnes and Egypt with 65,094 tonnes compared to 96,500 tonnes.

CHINA - Sugar imports in January continued on a rather low level reaching an overall total of only 7,687 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from 93,369 tonnes in December 1996 and 55,080 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (September/January) up to 429,355 tonnes compared to 1.167 mn tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.944 mn tonnes against 2.907 mn tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in September/January 1996/97 were Cuba with 132,590 tonnes raws against 168,953 tonnes, Australia with 228,793 tonnes against 326,995 tonnes and Thailand with 29,382 tonnes, sharply down from 236,453 tonnes.
The largest supplier of white sugar was South Korea with 14,786 tonnes against 13,565 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January 1997 amounted to 2,380 tonnes, sharply down from 118,266 tonnes in January 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/January up to 164,989 tonnes compared to 512,749 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 830,203 tonnes against 540,004 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in September/January 1996/97 were Pakistan with 62,499 tonnes whites against nil, Saudi Arabia with 39,481 tonnes, down from 129,749 tonnes and Hong Kong with 25,833 tonnes against 51,625 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 43,500 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 44.180 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on March 19. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to March 19 reached 1,679,950 tonnes, which compares to 1,722,198 tonnes last year.
